name: Chairul Tanjung
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2020)
forbes_bio: Chairul Tanjung's CT Corp. is best known for issuing credit cards, operating hypermarkets and running TV stations.
CT Corp's retail arm has grocery stores across Indonesia under the Transmart brand.
His group also controls the Wendy's franchise in Indonesia and owns the Versace, Mango and Jimmy Choo franchises.
He has a stake in Indonesian national carrier Garuda, which completed the restructuring of its $10 billion debt in late 2022.
The billionaire also owns a stake in Allo Bank Indonesia, one of the largest digital banks in the country.
forbes_facts: Chairul is the son of a journalist.
He sold study guides while attending school to become a dentist.

name: Frank VanderSloot
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Frank VanderSloot founded and runs Melaleuca, which makes more than 450 products ranging from health supplements to eco-friendly household cleaners.
Melaleuca sells direct from the factory to more than one million consumers every month through its online store.
Born into a poor farming family, VanderSloot ran the farm while his father worked a railroad job, then lived in a laundromat to pay his way through school.
He is a major landowner -- with an estimated 148,000 acres across Idaho, Utah and Montana -- and he runs a leading purebred angus cattle operation.
He is also an active political donor, giving millions to Republicans. He was a national finance co-chair for Mitt Romney's two presidential bids.
forbes_facts: VanderSloot is an avid indoor rower and holds six world records.
In 2019, VanderSloot started what is now a $1 million fund to help Idahoans defend themselves from aggressive medical debt collection tactics.

name: Park Hyeon-joo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Park Hyeon-joo founded Mirae Asset Global Investments (formerly called Mirae Asset Investment Advisory) and a venture capital affiliate in 1997.
He is known as the father of South Korea's mutual fund industry and launched the country's first closed-end mutual fund in 1998.
Now operating in 16 markets, his firm has approximately $272 billion in assets under management.
forbes_facts: The Mirae Asset Park Hyeon Joo Foundation provides scholarships to academically promising students from disadvantaged families.
In 2010, the Harvard Business School selected Mirae for a case study for its M.B.A. program.

name: Beda Diethelm
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Beda Diethelm is Swiss hearing aid manufacturer Sonova's largest individual shareholder, with a 10% stake.
Diethelm joined what would become Sonova in 1965, receiving a chunk of equity from the former owner in 1980.
Sonova has sales of roughly $2.8 billion and is based in Stafa, Switzerland and has production facilities in Vietnam and China.
Born in the tiny village of Galgenen, Switzerland, Diethelm first dabbled in electronics as an apprentice for a radio and TV technician in Zurich.
By 1962, Diethelm had become the head of production and technical director of Bommer, a Zurich company that was a global supplier of hearing aids.

name: T.Y. Tsai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025)
forbes_bio: T.Y. Tsai's father, Tsai Wan-lin, built Cathay Life Insurance into a powerhouse and was Taiwan's richest person at the time of his 2004 death.
Tsai struck out on his own in 2010, selling his shares in Cathay Financial Holding, Cathay Life's successor, to his brothers.
These days Tsai makes real estate investments through Homax Equity.
He has a collection of cars and art, including at least one Monet.
Brothers Hong-tu and Cheng-ta and cousins Daniel and Richard are all billionaires.

name: Toto Wolff
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2023)
forbes_bio: Toto Wolff is team principal and CEO of the Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula 1 Team. He controls 33%.
Under his direction, Mercedes claimed eight consecutive Formula 1 Constructor's Championships from, 2014 to 2021, as well as seven consecutive Drivers' Championships during that span.
Wolff started as a banker, later shifting to investing by founding incubator-style venture companies Marchfifteen in 1998 and Marchsixteen in 2004.
In 2009, Wolff invested in the Williams F1 team and played a key role in their win at the Spanish Grand Prix in 2012.
forbes_facts: At 17, Wolff embarked on his own short-lived racing career, competing in Austrian Formula Ford. It ended just three years later.
Wolff returned to racing in 2002, winning once in the FIA GT World Championship. He later claimed top honors at the 24 Hours of Bahrain.

name: Chen Tei-fu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Tei-Fu and his wife, Oi-Lin Chen, cofounded herbal-products maker Sunrider, which is now led by their five children.
Sunrider products are distributed in nearly 50 countries through a mix of franchises and company-owned stores.
He owns Sunworld-branded hotels in Beijing; the SLS Hotel in Beverly Hills, California; and St. Ermin's Hotel in London.
Chen's vast collection of Chinese art is on display at Sunrider headquarters in Torrance, California, near Los Angeles.
forbes_facts: In 1975 he was a starving college student in Utah, buying 20-cent hamburgers by the bunch at a weekly promotion so he could freeze them to eat later on.
His given name, Tei-Fu, means "receiving a fortune." He says his 19 grandchildren are his biggest fortune.

name: Xu Shugen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Xu Shugen is the founder and chairman of Shanghai-listed Zhejiang Dingli Machinery.
Founded in 2005, Dingli manufactures industrial lifts.
Xu's brother, Xu Zhilong, is a board member.

name: Yao Liangsong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Yao Liangsong is the chairman of Guangzhou-headquartered Oppein Home Group, one of China's largest makers of custom kitchen cabinets and home furniture.
Yao set up Oppein in 1994, which has prospered amid a rise in home ownership and growth in the middle class.
The company has opened 7,400 stores in more than 100 countries.
His brother Yao Liangbo is a director at Oppein.
forbes_facts: Yao holds a bachelor's degree in machinery manufacturing from Beihang University.

name: Ishay Davidi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Ishay Davidi is the Chairman, CEO, and founder of FIMI Opportunity Funds, Israel's first and largest private equity firm in terms of assets under management.
Since 1996, FIMI has raised seven private equity funds (three of which are currently active), with over $4.3 billion in capital commitments.
It has also completed 108 investments and 76 exits, generating over $9 billion in transaction value.
FIMI specializes in acquiring and scaling mature Israeli and Israel-related companies across diverse sectors, including automotive, electronics, aviation, energy, and logistics.

name: Arvind Lal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun India (2016-2021)
forbes_bio: Arvind Lal is executive chairman of diagnostics chain, Dr Lal PathLabs, in which he owns a majority stake.
The company is located in Gurgaon, a thriving township close to Delhi, and has clinical labs and collection centres across India.
The company offers a range of pathology, radiology and cardiology tests.
The business was founded  by his father S.K. Lal, also a doctor, in 1949 in Delhi. Arvind Lal joined the business after studying medicine, at age 28.
His wife, Vandana Lal, who is a pathologist, is the technical director and heads clinical research services and the test development department.
forbes_facts: Lal is a published author whose book, 'Corporate Yogi: My Journey as a Spiritual Seeker and an Accidental Entrepreneur' was published in 2018.
Lal has an honorary brigadier's rank in the Armed Forces Medical Services.

name: Mehmet Aydinlar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Mehmet Ali Aydinlar is founder and leader of Turkey's largest chain of private hospitals, Acibadem Healthcare Group.
He build the company after starting out as a consultant in the same field, took it public in 2000, and brought in a partner, Abraaj Capital, in 2008.
The company was delisted in 2012, after Aydinlar struck a deal with Malaysia's sovereign wealth fund and Kuala Lumpur-based IHH Healthcare Berhad.
Aydinlar exchanged Acibadem shares for cash and stock in IHH. He still owns 10% of Acibadem and serves as chairman of its board of directors.
Acibadem has been expanding into the Netherlands, Bulgaria, Macedonia, Serbia and Iraq.
forbes_facts: Aydinlar has been buying real estate since his days as a consultant for hire. In 2019, he was named Entrepreneur of the Year in Turkey by Ernst & Young.
His primary philanthropic undertaking is Istanbul-based Acibadem University, whose mission is to advance healthcare in Turkey through education and research.
